Focus directory identity vs display selectors and persistence, dual manifests, package/artifact/product distinction, authority and crash recovery, cohesion after four-crate consolidation. No. Once the local tag exists, the next bare `callisto release` skips that package—even if its forge release is incomplete. This concern applies to both #167 and #168; the relevant selection and ordering code is unchanged.

| Step | Confirmed code evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Tag lands before forge creation | `ForgeRelease` depends on the package’s tag operation. [derive.rs:418](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/derive.rs:418) |
| Retry recalculates the roster | The local route reloads the workspace and calls `derive_unreleased_decision`. [local.rs:95](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/local.rs:95), [local.rs:105](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/local.rs:105) |
| Tagged versions are excluded | Selection immediately skips a tagged version; the predicate checks tag existence, not forge completion. [release_decision.rs:195](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:195), [release_decision.rs:251](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:251) |
| Empty roster reports success | If nothing else remains selected, the CLI prints “Nothing to release.” and exits successfully. [release.rs:69](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs:69) |

The resulting failure scenario is a high-confidence static inference: **tag succeeds → forge creation or publication fails → bare retry omits the unfinished package**. Explicit `--package` also cannot force completion: a tagged selection is rejected as `NotARelease`. [release_decision.rs:229](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release_decision.rs:229)

CI differs because committed-roster planning reads the decision, and execution validation retains `received.decision` instead of recalculating unreleased packages. The executor can then adopt the tag and attempt the remaining forge operation. [CLI release.rs:392](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-cli/src/commands/release.rs:392), [capability.rs:257](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/capability.rs:257)

A closely related case occurs when tag creation succeeds but its push fails: the local tag already exists and can suppress the next bare retry. [provider/tag.rs:72](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/provider/tag.rs:72)

This qualifies my earlier recovery assessment: the executor supports recovery with a retained roster; bare local reselection can lose that roster. No builds, tests, or writes performed.
